title: Musical saw
summary: A musical saw is an ordinary hand saw bent into a slow S-curve and drawn with a violin bow along its smooth edge. Where the blade bends the most, it sings a pure, wavering note that slides from pitch to pitch.
howToPlay: Eight places on the blade are lit, low notes near the handle and high notes toward the tip.
Play the place a closing ring marks. The bow rides the edge there and the blade sings.
Notes swell and hold, so start each one on time and let it ring until the next.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Players tune the blade by the curve they give it. The same saw can sing across more than two octaves, and its voice is much like a voice.
credits: Tradition: the musical saw; patterns written for this game
